summary: Paradise sits at roughly 1,800 feet on a forested ridge above the Sacramento Valley, which means summer highs average around 72°F while the flatland below bakes — a genuine elevation dividend that reshapes daily comfort from June through September. The town's 18.3 square miles at just 562 people per square mile give it a spread-out, semi-rural pacing where ponderosa pines outnumber stoplights, and the western edge offers long views down toward the valley floor. The Camp Fire of November 2018 destroyed approximately 90 percent of the town's structures, and the population data here — just over 10,000 — reflects a community still actively rebuilding, which is the defining context for nearly every metric. A median home value of $680,600 against a median household income of $106,250 produces a price-to-income ratio around 6.4×, notably steep for a rural foothill town, partly because new construction commands premium pricing on a constrained, fire-scarred landscape. Employment leans heavily on healthcare (Adventist Health Feather River hospital is the major anchor), education, and construction tied to the rebuild; most other professional employment means a winding 15-mile descent to Chico. With nine hours of daily sunshine on average and direct access to Butte Creek Canyon trails and the upper Sacramento Valley watershed, outdoor life is genuinely excellent — but the tradeoff is real: this is a town whose identity is inseparable from catastrophic wildfire risk, and every new roof goes up in that knowledge.
